entries.name: T-junction
entries.description: End-to-side meeting: stick A's end coordinate falls on stick B's centreline (within 1 mm tolerance).
entries.participants: Stud meeting top plate; stud meeting bottom plate; nog meeting stud; truss diagonal meeting chord.
emits: On B (the receiving stick): LipNotch centred on A's centreline + InnerDimple at the LipNotch position.
On A (the entering stick): no extra ops at this end — its standard end-cap rule already handles it.
entries.why: The lip of B must be relieved so A keys in cleanly without binding; the dimple gives the connection screw a target.

entries.name: X-crossing
entries.description: Two sticks' centreline projections intersect inside both bounding boxes.
entries.participants: Truss webs crossing each other (linear truss scissor joint); wall X-bracing in a brace bay; bottom-chord bolt cluster on a TB2B truss.
emits: On the longer / structural primary stick: LipNotch + InnerDimple at the crossing point.
On the shorter / secondary stick: typically nothing — the primary's notch accommodates the secondary's pass-through.
entries.why: When one stick crosses another at angle, only one of them needs the relief — the one carrying the connection.

entries.name: End-butt
entries.description: The end of one stick meets the end of another, both on the same line, with a small gap (≤30 mm).
entries.participants: Continuous plates split by a panel break; nog continuing across a stud (treated as two nogs after frame-context detection).
emits: On both sticks: standard end-cap operation (e.g. Swage for studs, LipNotch for plates) at each end. No special joint-specific operation.
entries.why: End-butts are framing convenience, not structural connections — the standard end-caps suffice.

entries.name: Lap
entries.description: Two sticks parallel within a tight angle threshold, with overlapping length, separated by less than one flange height (~41 mm).
entries.participants: Double-stud at panel join (pair at X and X+43); paired-header H1+H2 box header.
emits: On both sticks at the overlap zone: Web @8 mm slab-anchor pattern when at slab; otherwise no joint-specific operation (paired-header laps get standard Web stiffener distribution per Catalogue A).
Otherwise: nothing — passive lap, dealt with by adjacent structural connections.
entries.why: Laps are usually structural connection zones; the operation depends on what's being connected.

entries.name: B2B partner pair
entries.description: Two studs at the same x-position (within 1 mm), in the same frame, mirrored. Detected as a B2B context.
entries.participants: TB2B truss chords; double-jamb at large openings.
emits: Web @spacing on both studs: 7 holes spaced 447 mm, anchored 38 mm from each end.
All other operations standard per-stick.
entries.why: B2B pairs need additional fasteners at regular intervals because they share the load path.

entries.name: Header-cripple (Kb meets H)
entries.description: A Kb's upper end coincides with a header's underside.
entries.participants: Every cripple meeting a header from below — head-side corners of door/window openings.
emits: On H at the Kb's x-position: LipNotch + paired InnerDimple (the paired-dimple rule fires when the frame has paired headers).
On Kb's lower end: Chamfer @start (so it sits flat on the plate below).
On Kb's upper end: standard Swage + InnerDimple end-cap.
entries.why: The cripple is short and angled; it needs the chamfer to bear, and the header needs the notch + dimples for the cripple-to-header bolt.

entries.name: Truss-vertical-at-chord
entries.description: A truss-W (vertical, usage='web') meets a horizontal chord. Detected as a truss interaction (frame-type check: 'truss' in plan name).
entries.participants: Every interior vertical web on a TIN linear truss.
emits: On chord: LipNotch + InnerDimple at the W's centreline.
On W: TrussChamfer @start and TrussChamfer @end (truss webs always get truss-chamfer at both ends, irrespective of angle).
entries.why: The truss-chamfer is the manufacturer-specified end-cut for truss webs; the chord notch is identical to the wall T-junction rule but flagged for truss processing.

entries.name: Truss-diagonal-at-chord
entries.description: A truss-W meets a chord at an angle. Use line-intersection in the XZ plane to find the meeting point, project to chord y-level, convert to local position along the chord.
entries.participants: Every diagonal web on every truss.
emits: On chord at the projected point: LipNotch + InnerDimple.
On W: TrussChamfer at both ends; Swage @end with span = 39 / cos(angle), capped at 200 mm.
entries.why: Diagonal webs need the same chord notch but their own end-spans depend on cut angle.

entries.name: Wall-W-at-plate
entries.description: A wall-W brace stick (not a truss web — wall-frame, not truss-frame) hits a plate at angle ≥28° from vertical.
entries.participants: The X-brace in a wall brace bay (typically L1/L3 first and last bays).
emits: On plate at the meeting point: LipNotch + InnerDimple.
On W at this end: Chamfer (wall-style chamfer, not TrussChamfer) + Swage 41 mm + InnerDimple @10 mm.
entries.why: Wall braces use a different chamfer geometry from truss webs; the angle threshold prevents the chamfer firing on near-vertical W's that don't need it.

entries.name: Linear-truss-web-at-chord
entries.description: Variant of Truss-vertical-at-chord and Truss-diagonal-at-chord that fires when the HYTEK Linear-truss simplifier's 4-layer gate matches: frame.type === 'Truss' AND plan name matches /-LIN-/i AND every stick is 89×41 LC 0.75 gauge AND frame has both chord+web members. The simplifier's centreline-intersection rule rewrites the joint.
entries.participants: Every chord-web crossing on a HYTEK Linear truss (89×41 LC 0.75, plan name contains '-LIN-'). Both vertical webs and angled diagonals.
emits: On the WEB of EACH stick at the CL–CL crossing: 3 × M6 BOLT HOLES at 17 mm pitch perpendicular to (i.e. drilled through) the web. The 3-hole pattern is along the stick's length axis at the crossing position.
Strips/replaces the FrameCAD-baseline outputs at this joint: NO LipNotch on chord, NO Swage on web, NO InnerDimple. The BOLT HOLES rule is the ONLY joint-specific operation.
TrussChamfer at both ends of the W stays from the FrameCAD baseline (the simplifier doesn't touch chamfers).
entries.why: Linear trusses use back-to-back web contact at every joint with 3 × M6 self-drilling screws — a fundamentally different connection pattern from the FrameCAD-baseline LipNotch/Swage/InnerDimple triple. STRICT ISOLATION: this rule must NEVER fire on walls, floors, non-LIN trusses, or non-89×41 designs. Walls and other trusses use the regular Truss-diagonal-at-chord / Truss-vertical-at-chord rules (LipNotch + Swage + InnerDimple).

entries.name: Linear-truss-boxed-chord-segment
entries.description: Two 89×41 C-sections nested mouth-to-mouth to form a closed-tube boxed member on a high-load segment of a Linear-truss chord. The Box piece is shorter than the parent (only spans the high-moment zone) and a single chord can have multiple Box zones (e.g. B1 (Box1) + B1 (Box2)). Fires only on Linear trusses.
entries.participants: High-load segments of any chord on a HYTEK Linear truss (89×41 LC 0.75, plan name contains '-LIN-'). The parent runs the chord's full length; the Box piece is a separate member only as long as the boxed zone.
emits: Paired flange dimples on Box AND parent at matching world positions: outward-pressed on Box's flanges, inward-pressed on parent's flanges. The bumps interlock at the flange-to-flange seam (geometric self-registration; operator measures nothing).
10g-16mm flathead screw at every paired-dimple position. Countersunk so the head sits flush with the flange face. Passes through Box flange (0.75) + parent flange (0.75) = 1.5 mm steel grip.

Spacing rule (canonical 2026-05-10): first/last dimple = 15 mm from each end of the Box piece; maximum gap between adjacent dimples = 900 mm. Both pieces get matching dimples at the same world positions.
entries.why: Boxed segment gives ~3-4× the section modulus and much higher buckling/torsion resistance over the boxed length only — a localised strength upgrade where the chord's bending moment peaks. The dimples self-align the Box on the parent during slide-in; the screws make the connection permanent. STRICT ISOLATION: this rule fires ONLY on LIN trusses + 89×41 LC 0.75. Wall B2B partner pairs (also flange-on-flange geometrically) use the Web @8 slab-anchor pattern and alternating-side screws per FC-W3 — a different rule.
